q: What calorific value should I use for furnace oil, kerosene and petrol in kcal per kg?
title: Calorific value of oils in kcal per kg
short: PPAC's Ready Reckoner lists average calorific values of 10,440 kcal per kg for fuel oil, 10,638 for kerosene, 11,135 for motor gasoline and 12,135 for NGL. Multiply by 4.19 to get kJ. Use these for energy totals when the supplier gives no test value.
audience: Energy managers filling BRSR energy tables or boiler records

ul: Fuel oil: 10,440 kcal per kg, about 43.7 GJ per tonne.
Kerosene: 10,638 kcal per kg, about 44.6 GJ per tonne.
Motor gasoline: 11,135 kcal per kg, about 46.7 GJ per tonne.

p: PPAC labels these average international calorific values without saying gross or net. Values in this range are typically gross. IPCC emission factors are per unit of net energy, so for CO2 use mass times the IPCC per-kg factor, and use these values for energy reporting with the basis stated.
BRSR asks for total energy in joules. Tonnes of each fuel times a calorific value gives that figure, and stating the source makes it checkable.
